Definition: from G3844 and G2192; to hold near, i.e. present, afford, exhibit, furnish occasion:--bring, do, give, keep, minister, offer, shew, + trouble.
BiblicalUsage: Parecho means to hold near, to present, to afford, to give. Demetrius the silversmith brings no small gain to the craftsmen in Acts 19:24, and the barbarians show no little kindness to the shipwrecked in Acts 28:2. Paul tells masters in Colossians 4:1 to give their servants what is just and equal, and in 1 Timothy 6:17 he says God gives us richly all things to enjoy.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe what a person gives away shows what he holds near: Demetrius held his gain, the islanders held out kindness, and God holds out everything richly. My position is that the giving that counts is the giving that costs, and God has already given first.
